Leave-one-out banks

Source: R/bank.R
bank_loo.Rd

Refits the bank once per scored participant, each time excluding that participant's own measurements. This restores the honesty condition when no external donor sample exists, at the cost of one fit per participant.

Usage

bank_loo(loglik, lambda = 1, nu = NULL, ...)

Arguments

loglik

A participant-by-candidate log-likelihood matrix.

lambda

Entropy penalty passed to fit_bank().

nu

Optional per-participant candidate retention count. When supplied, screen_candidates() is rerun inside every leave-one-out fold using only that fold's donors. This is required when support screening is data-dependent; screening once on the full cohort before calling bank_loo() would leak the held-out participant into its bank.

...

Further arguments to fit_bank().

Value

A list with weights, a participant-by-candidate matrix whose row i holds the bank fitted without participant i, and the corresponding logLik, a vector of each participant's log class likelihood under their own leave-one-out bank, and support_size, the number of candidates retained in each fold.

Details

The columns of loglik must come from a candidate family fixed independently of the participant being scored. If the family is reduced using participant measurements, pass nu here so screening is repeated within each fold. Positivity or other screens that depend only on the mechanistic design, and not on participant measurements, may be applied before this function.

See also

fit_bank()
